picks.what: The cathedral, photochrom print (Library of Congress)
picks.why: the black lava-stone cathedral with its new spires (finished 1884), the city’s emblem; color, high resolution

picks.what: View over the rooftops to the Michelin works, photograph (ETH Library, Zurich)
picks.why: general view of the town with the Michelin factory chimneys that defined it in the 20th century; trimmed black frame and caption strip

picks.what: The old town and the cathedral, photograph
picks.why: general view from a height with the black cathedral towering over the old town and the hills behind

gaps: P0, P1, P2: no candidates. P3: only #1 (Delécluze, 1821), a wash drawing of the Monts Dôme in which the city is a faint speck — not recognizable, skipped.
notes: #2 date: LOC gives 1890 for this Photoglob series, used as ‘1890s’. P4 alternative: Notre-Dame-du-Port photochrom (#3), also portrait format. #4–#7 are the Puy de Dôme, its temple ruins and Tournoël castle, not the city. #8–#10 Mittelholzer aerials show countryside and the volcano, not the town. P6 alternative: #15 (2023, from the Ferris wheel over Place de Jaude, cathedral and Puy de Dôme, sharper light but foreground buildings dominate).
